 Putnam County to give out sandbags amid rainy weather conditions
 Chris Will , News4JAX reporter , Jacksonville 
 Published:  November 19, 2026 at 3:35 PM Updated:  November 19, 2026 at 4:03 PM Tags:  Putnam County , Weather Rain Flooding Flood Storm Preparing Sand Bags Sandbags Sand Bagging PUTNAM COUNTY, Fla. – Residents bracing for a wet week can now pick up free sandbags at three locations across Putnam County as heavy rain and flooding threaten the area through the weekend and beyond.
 The National Weather Service is forecasting 3 to 4 inches of rain on the eastern side of the county, with localized higher amounts possible. Flash flooding is a concern — particularly in urban areas and low-lying spots that tend to hold water — as heavier rain bands move through.
 Recommended Videos
 Where to get sandbags
 Three self-serve sandbag sites are open now. Bring your own shovel.
 Bostwick VFD — 110 Mulberry St., Palatka 
 Riverside VFD — 101 Gail Dr., Satsuma 
 Welaka — 51 Sportsman Dr., Welaka 
 LIVE RADAR | Weather Authority Alert issued for elevated flooding risk from rounds of windy rain Today through Friday 
 St. Johns River expected to rise for weeks
 The flooding threat extends well beyond this week. Rainfall totals to the south of Putnam County, combined with astronomical high tides, are expected to push the St. Johns River and its tributaries to moderate to major flood levels over the next two weeks.
 Residents who live near the river or its tributaries should monitor conditions closely and take precautions now.
 Steffen Turnipseed, Putnam County’s chief of emergency operations and preparedness, urged residents to stay informed and take the threat seriously.
 “Stay in touch with what’s going on with the news and the weather,” Turnipseed said. “Don’t blow this off. This could be an event that gets worse over time.”
 Turnipseed said the county was not expecting to call evacuations, but cautioned that conditions can change quickly — and that residents should not wait to be told to act.
 “Have a plan to go somewhere else. Don’t wait for us to tell you to do that,” he said.
 He also urged neighbors to look out for one another. “See if they need anything, have a plan put together. Be prepared,” Turnipseed said.
 County-wide updates are available on Facebook at facebook.com/PutnamCountyEM .
